what_happened: A queued page item (8wqq) was written against a version of the page that had since changed by two fixes. It failed twice. The drain stopped on it as a repeated failure. The operator closed the stale item by hand because Athena has no way to retire a queued item that has gone stale. No job was attached to the event.
cause: Queued items are treated as valid until they run. Nothing records which version of the target they were written against, and nothing compares that version with the current one before running. The drain's repeated-failure stop is a halt with no recovery path: it does not set the item aside or ask whether it is still wanted. So an item that has gone stale can only be removed by an operator acting outside the lifecycle. The same missing exit appears in the stuck-job case, where close and retry both refused.
prevention: Record the target's base revision (such as the page's commit or content hash) when an item is queued. Before each run, and again when the drain meets a repeated failure, compare it with the current revision. If the target has changed, mark the item stale and park it. Parking is a sanctioned state that the drain skips, and a command can move the item out of it (retire or requeue). The drain then continues past it and reports it, instead of halting. Also require that every queue state has at least one command that leaves it, so no hand-closing is needed.
proposed_request: Make Athena's queue handle stale items without operator intervention. When an item is queued, record the revision of the page or file it targets. Before running an item, and when the drain hits a repeated failure, compare that revision with the current one. If the target has changed since the item was written, mark the item stale, skip it, and let the drain carry on with the remaining items. Report the stale item in the drain output. Add a command to retire a stale item or requeue it against the current revision. Show that a stale item whose page has had two later fixes is parked and does not stop the drain. Also show that no queue state exists from which neither retire nor requeue works.
